World.title: FACT CHECK: Photos of Duterte being assisted in ICC courtroom are AI-generated
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

Duterte has not made any in-person appearances during the recent hearings on his crimes against humanity charges. He was also absent during the first status conference on his case on May 27.

Claim: Photos show International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III Presiding Judge Joanna Korner and defense lawyer Peter Haynes assisting former president Rodrigo Duterte inside the ICC courtroom.

Rating: FALSE

Why we fact-checked this: Multiple posts circulated on social media showing the photos of Duterte wearing a brown suit and looking weak while being assisted in the courtroom by Korner and Haynes. A post bearing the claim was posted on June 1, 2026, and has since garnered over 5,900 reactions, 1,100 comments, and 371 shares.

The caption on the post reads, “Pakiramdam ko malapit kana makalaya tatay Digong konting tiis nalang makakauwi kana din mahal kong pangulo hinding hindi ka pababayaan ng Panginoon dahil busilak ang iyong puso mahal na mahal ka ng milyon-milyong pilipino sa buong mundo.”

(I feel like you’re about to be free, Tatay Digong. Just a little patience and you’ll be able to go home, my dear president. The Lord will never abandon you because your heart is pure. Millions of Filipinos around the world love you very much).

A similar claim posted on June 7, 2026, turned the photos into a Facebook reel and has also received 82,000 views. The post pertains to Duterte’s weak posture based on the photos, implying that he should be free from detention because of his deteriorating health condition.

“Kaluoy sa amahan sa katawhan nganong Dili nlng hatagan ug kagawasan,” the caption said. (Have mercy on the father of the people, why don’t you just give them freedom?)

The post pertains to Duterte’s posture in the photos, implying that he should be free from detention because of his deteriorating health condition.

The facts: The photos are fake and were generated using artificial intelligence (AI). Sight Engine, an AI detection software, flagged one of the photos as 99% AI-generated. Hive Moderation also flagged the photo as 99.9% likely to contain AI-generated content. Truth Scan also flagged the image as 97% AI-generated.

The AI-generated photos also show wrong depictions of the ICC banner. It falsely shows the horizontal line between “International Criminal” and “International Court.” The text on the ICC banner and logo actually reads “Cour Pénale Internationale” above the horizontal line and “International Criminal Court” below it.

Reverse image search also did not show any real photos similar to the AI-generated images.

Duterte appearance: Duterte has not made any in-person appearances in any of the recent hearings related to his crimes against humanity charges because of his administration’s war on drugs, which reportedly resulted in over 30,000 deaths.

On May 27, 2026, Duterte was also absent during his case’s first status conference after he waived his right to appear at the hearing. In February 2026, Duterte also waived his right to attend the pre-trial hearing, saying that he is “old, tired, and frail,” a reason which the ICC described as irrelevant.

His last appearance in ICC hearings was on March 14, 2025, through video link from the ICC detention center, during the identity verification of the Pre-Trial Chamber I.

The ICC allowed Duterte’s past absences on the basis of a waiver. According to the ICC judges and under ICC rules, a waiver is sufficient to be excused from proceedings. While the ICC has allowed these in the past, Duterte’s attendance will be mandatory on November 30, which marks the start of the full trial for his case.

Debunked: Rappler has debunked similar false claims about Duterte’s ICC detention:

– Angelee Kaye Abelinde/Rappler.com

Angelee Kaye Abelinde is a student journalist based in Naga City, and an alumna of Rappler’s Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

World.title: No sanctions yet as UAAP to ‘go where evidence leads’ in Ateneo drowning incident
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

‘We cannot pass judgment this early,’ says UAAP executive director Rebo Saguisag as the league gathers information and waits for official reports on the deaths of Ateneo basketball players Rene Baterbonia and Divine Adili

MANILA, Philippines – UAAP executive director Rebo Saguisag on Wednesday, June 10, said the league will “go where the evidence leads” before handing down sanctions to those responsible for the deaths of Ateneo basketball players Rene Baterbonia and Divine Adili.

Baterbonia and Adili died from drowning on Monday, June 8, during the Blue Eagles’ team building at a private resort in Dipaculao, Aurora.

Aurora police found no indication of foul play, describing the deaths of the two young big men a “natural accident” based on accounts of people who were with Baterbonia and Adili.

Meanwhile, Ateneo has coordinated with the National Bureau Investigation and the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group following the request of Baterbonia’s parents to have his remains autopsied.

Play Video

“We cannot pass judgment this early,” Saguisag said in a press conference organized by the sports stakeholders’ panel composed of the UAAP, Philippine Sports Commission, Commission on Higher Education, Department of Education, Samahang Basketbol ng Pilipinas, and National Youth Commission, when asked whether Ateneo will take part in the upcoming Season 89.

“Not to trivialize what happened, but elementary due process states that everyone should be heard. The expertise of each agency should be considered.”

“We are now in the process of gathering information, waiting for official reports that have been undergoing.”

The Blue Eagles, mentored by multi-titled head coach Tab Baldwin, have held similar team building activities at the same resort for years, according to Aurora police.

Asked whether Baldwin will be suspended by the UAAP, Saguisag said it is up to Ateneo to penalize the 68-year-old tactician.

“We have to go where the evidence leads,” said Saguisag.

Baterbonia, Adili, and other Ateneo players, the police said, were in thigh-deep water before they found themselves in a deeper section and got swept away by strong currents.

Contrary to speculations that spread on social media, no weights were found attached to the bodies of Baterbonia and Adili, as confirmed by the rescuers and members of the Blue Eagles’ coaching staff.

“I asked them, from one coach to another, and they said the players were not asked to wear weights,” said Jess Evangelio, Baterbonia’s high school coach at the Ateneo de Davao. – Rappler.com

World.title: In AI-made video, Trump mimics Naruto, but misses the point entirely
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

Naruto Uzumaki and Donald Trump are wildly different character types and implying Trump is a Naruto figure is completely out of place

US President Donald Trump and Seventh Hokage of the Hidden Leaf Village Naruto Uzumaki are two different sorts of leaders born from different types of circumstances, but you’d be hard-pressed to suss out who’s the fictional one if a recent AI-generated video of Trump is to be believed.

Over on Truth Social, Trump on Saturday, June 6, posted an artificial intelligence-produced video of himself being adored by various nations and nationalities. In the short Japanese segment of the video, with “I love Donald, Donald Trump” blaring in the background, Trump appears onscreen in the familiar jumpsuit of Naruto Uzumaki, doing the fictional ninja’s famous kage bunshin, or shadow cloning technique.

Posing as famous people is not an unfamiliar look for Trump, as he had already likened himself to a doctor-like Christ figure previously. But inasmuch as Christians hate the comparison between Trump and Jesus, you cannot expect fans of a beloved Japanese cultural phenomenon to not raise an eyebrow at the sight of Donald Naruto-Trumping on social media, or not alluding to the somewhat blatant copyright infringement.

There is another reason why Trump’s short stint as Naruto stings, however, and that’s because Naruto and Trump are wildly different character types, and implying Trump is a Naruto figure is completely incongruent.

Naruto starts off shunned by his village by virtue of hosting a malevolent demonic fox inside of him, and seeks attention in his youth by being rambunctious and trouble-seeking until he is trained by his elders to better understand himself and his circumstances. While flawed, Naruto struggles and tries to make up for his flaws, with his own use of the shadow-cloning technique coming as the result of harnessing the demonic fox inside his body.

Through many growth events in his life, Naruto becomes the leader of that same village, beloved and respected by his peers as he guides his village through a time of postwar peace.

Donald Trump seems to be stuck in the childhood phase of troublemaking — even without a malevolent fox demon hiding inside him. A different sort of leader, Trump has started or exacerbated wars, and backtracks or lies when needed to suit his fancy.

As an NBC News video showed, Trump also storms out of uncomfortable conversations and attacks his detractors constantly.

Trump is not, in comparison to Naruto, an exemplary leader.

If there’s one key takeaway from all these, it’s this: Trump can’t do a shadow-cloning technique, since he’s not an adept fictional ninja, but a stunted manchild reminiscent of Naruto as a kid. – Rappler.com

World.title: Navotas fishers renew call to stop Manila Bay reclamation
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines — Fisherfolk in Navotas marked World Oceans Day on June 8 with a protest against ongoing reclamation projects in Manila Bay, saying the developments continue to threaten livelihoods, coastal communities and marine ecosystems despite a government suspension on reclamation activities.

Members of the Navotas chapter of Pambansang Lakas ng Kilusang Mamamalakaya ng Pilipinas, or PAMALAKAYA, gathered at C4 Centennial Park to oppose several projects in the bay, including the 650-hectare Navotas Coastal Bay Reclamation Project being undertaken by San Miguel Corp. in partnership with the local government of Navotas City.

Article continues after this 

The group said the project has already affected local mussel farmers whose structures were dismantled starting in 2024 to make way for reclamation activities.

“Higit dalawang taon nang halos walang makain ang aming mga pamilya buhat nang tanggalin ang aming mga tahungan dahil sa reklamasyon. Dapat ibalik ang pangunahing kabuhayan sa dagat at tuluyan nang ipatigil ang mga mapanirang proyektong ito,” said Romel Escarial, president of Pamalakaya-Navotas.

(For more than two years now, our families have had little to eat after our mussel farms were removed because of the reclamation project. Our primary livelihood from the sea must be restored, and these destructive projects must be stopped once and for all.)

Pamalakaya said the reclamation project, which it linked to the New Manila International Airport project in Bulacan, continues to raise concerns about displacement, worsening floods and environmental degradation.

The fisherfolk group also criticized the Philippine Reclamation Authority, or PRA, accusing it of moving to resume at least two reclamation projects in Manila Bay despite the suspension announced by the national government in 2023.

Article continues after this 

“Nagkukumahog ang PRA na magpatuloy ang reklamasyon at binabalewala ang umiiral na suspensyon at ang pag-aaral ng mga eksperto kaugnay sa masamang dulot nito. Hindi natapos ang pinsalang dulot ng reklamasyon sa kabuhayan ng maraming mangingisda sa Manila Bay. Maging ang mga malaganap na pagbaha sa kalakhang Maynila at mga karatig na probinsya ay dahil sa mga naturang proyekto,” said Fernando Hicap, national chair of Pamalakaya.

(The PRA is scrambling to push reclamation projects forward while disregarding the existing suspension and the findings of experts on their harmful impacts. The damage caused by reclamation to the livelihoods of many fisherfolk in Manila Bay has not ended. Even the widespread flooding in Metro Manila and nearby provinces is a result of these projects.)

Article continues after this 

READ: Pamalakaya to DENR: Uphold suspension order on Manila Bay reclamation

The group maintained that the suspension should remain in force, citing the cumulative impact assessment commissioned by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources, or DENR, which found significant environmental and socioeconomic risks associated with reclamation activities in Manila Bay.

The DENR-backed study, released in 2025, examined the cumulative effects of reclamation projects around the bay and found that reclamation activities disrupt the natural circulation of water, weaken water exchange and contribute to the buildup of sediments, pollutants and debris.

Scientists also warned that these changes could worsen flooding, degrade water quality and affect fishing grounds.

According to the study, around 6,100 hectares of new land could be created from 21 reclamation projects in various stages of development around Manila Bay — an area nearly equivalent to the combined land area of Manila and Marikina.

READ: 21 Manila Bay reclamation projects equal area of 2 cities

Researchers also reported that reclamation activities reduce fishing grounds and damage critical habitats such as mangroves, which serve as natural barriers against storm surges, typhoons and coastal erosion.

Despite environmental pressures, the same study found that Manila Bay remains an active and productive fishing ground.

From April to October 2024, fisherfolk in Manila Bay recorded average catches of 2 to 4 kilograms of fish per hour, higher than the 1 to 2 kilograms per hour recorded in several other fishing areas surveyed by researchers.

Previous studies have likewise pointed to the bay’s ecological significance.

Manila Bay spans about 199,400 hectares and supports more than 50 species of fish and at least eight species of shellfish. It is also considered an important spawning area for sardines and remains one of the country’s major fishing grounds for small-scale fishers.

READ: Manila Bay not dead, but reclamation killing it, say groups

Concerns over Navotas project

The Navotas Coastal Bay Reclamation Project has long been opposed by fisherfolk groups.

Data previously cited from the PRA showed that the project covers about 650 hectares and has been promoted as a mixed-use development that would include socialized housing, commercial areas, parks, public facilities and other infrastructure.

Supporters of the project have described it as a key component of future development in Navotas and as a potential southern gateway to the New Manila International Airport in Bulacan.

But Pamalakaya has argued that the project threatens the livelihoods of fisherfolk and fish workers dependent on Manila Bay.

The group previously estimated that the dismantling of more than 200 mussel farms and other fishing structures could affect at least 1,000 small-scale fishers, fish workers and operators of stationary fish traps.

READ: Navotas fishers plead for permanent ban on reclamation

https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1819658/navotas-fishers-plead-for-permanent-ban-on-reclamation

In earlier statements, Pamalakaya said some affected fishers had already experienced sharp declines in income following the removal of mussel farms and fishing structures.

The organization also pointed to other reclamation projects that it said continue to move forward despite the government’s suspension, including a reclamation project in Bacoor City, Cavite.

Environmental groups have repeatedly called for Manila Bay to be declared a reclamation-free zone.

In previous campaigns, they warned that dozens of proposed and approved reclamation projects could affect tens of thousands of hectares of fishing grounds and coastal habitats around the bay.

For Pamalakaya, World Oceans Day served as an opportunity to renew calls for the permanent cancellation of reclamation projects that it considers destructive.

The group urged the government to protect fishing grounds and marine ecosystems while safeguarding the livelihoods of small-scale fishers and coastal communities that depend on Manila Bay for food and income. /dm

World.title: Fair long weekend weather expected as ‘habagat’ to further weaken
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines — The southwest monsoon or “habagat” is expected to weaken even further over the long weekend for Independence Day, June 12, indicating possible fairer weather, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said.

Habagat refers to warm, moist winds originating from the southwest, which bring rains to the western portion of the Philippines.

“Over the long weekend, tomorrow, habagat will continue to weaken and will only affect the western portion of Northern Luzon, where cloudy skies are expected, Pagasa weather specialist Leanne Loreto said

Article continues after this 

“By Saturday until Monday, fair weather is expected,” she added.

Loreto, however, said sudden but brief rain showers due to thunderstorms, flooding and landslides over the weekend are possible in the eastern part of Southern Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao. /gsg

World.title: Warm, humid Thursday as ‘habagat’ weakens
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines — It will be a warm and humid Thursday in most of the country as the southwest monsoon or “habagat” weakens, according to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa).

Cloudy skies and scattered rain showers, however, are expected in Ilocos Norte, Batanes and the Babuyan Islands, Pagasa weather specialist Leanne Loreto said.

“Other parts of our country, including Metro Manila, will be partly cloudy to cloudy. So expect warm and humid conditions today,” she said in Filipino.

Article continues after this 

Thunderstorms are expected in Eastern Visayas as well as Mindanao after midday, Loreto added.

In its latest weather bulletin, Pagasa also reported that no low-pressure area and / or tropical cyclone were spotted in and around the Philippine re of responsibility.

No gale warning was likewise raised over any of the country’s seaboards. /gsg

World.title: Fire hits Valenzuela City transport hub, reaches 3rd alarm
World.content:
Fire breaks out at the Valenzuela Gateway Complex on Thursday morning, June 11, 2026, as seen in this video taken from the East Service Road along Northern Luzon Expressway in Valenzuela City. (Screengrab from video courtesy Dianne Ulan-Lumarlan)

MANILA, Philippines — Fire broke out at the Valenzuela Gateway Complex (VGC) on Thursday morning, reaching up to the third alarm, according to the Bureau of Fire Protection National Capital Region (BFP NCR).

The blaze involved a commercial area at the transit hub in Paso de Blas, Valenzuela City, the BFP NCR said in its initial incident report.

READ: Fire breaks out in residential area in Intramuros

Article continues after this 

The fire reached third alarm at 5:59 a.m., the regional fire bureau noted.

The fire was declared under control at 7:11 a.m., according to the BFP NCR.

A third alarm requires the response of at least 12 fire trucks.

The BFP NCR has yet to determine the cause of the fire, number of possible injuries and cost of damage to property. /gsg

World.title: SC junks taxpayer suit over Senate row
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines — The Supreme Court on Wednesday junked for “lack of legal standing” the petition of high school teacher Barry Tayam to validate the June 3 Senate session that led to a reshuffle in the chamber and the installation of acting Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian.

In a 20-page petition for certiorari, taxpayer and voter Tayam asked the high court on June 5 to intervene in the Senate leadership standoff by finding grave abuse of discretion in the acts of the bloc led by Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano and affirming the leadership of Gatchalian.

Article continues after this 

But the high tribunal, in a statement, said that Tayam “failed to show that he suffered or was at risk of imminent suffering or direct injury” from the acts of Cayetano and Senators Pia Cayetano and Loren Legarda, the respondents in the case.

The Supreme Court has yet to release a full copy of its ruling.

READ: High school teacher urges SC to affirm Senate quorum

The Cayetano siblings and Legarda were among the 10-member bloc that deliberately skipped sessions for three straight days from June 1 to June 3. They also refused to recognize the leadership of Gatchalian, who was elected by a quorum consisting of 12 senators on June 3.

Alan Peter Cayetano was elected Senate President on May 11 after Sen. Ronald dela Rosa emerged from hiding after more than six months to support the coup against then Senate President Vicente “Tito” Sotto III.

Article continues after this 

Legarda was named Senate President Pro Tempore while Pia Cayetano was appointed the blue ribbon committee chair.

Independent filer

Tayam, who has been a constant petitioner in the high court over various issues, earlier denied being backed or sponsored by anybody in filing the case.

Article continues after this 

READ: SC should stay out of Senate leadership row, law expert says

He cited in his petition the Supreme Court’s landmark decision in 1949 on Avelino v. Cuenco, the only case tackled by the high court involving the question of what constitutes a Senate quorum.

The Gatchalian-led bloc had cited the case and a 2015 Senate precedent to declare that the presence of 12 senators constituted a majority as there were only 22 senators over whom the Senate could obtain jurisdiction.

This was after Dela Rosa went back into hiding on May 14 after the International Criminal Court issued a warrant for his arrest as a “coperpetrator” in the Duterte drug war. Sen. Jinggoy Estrada, meanwhile, was arrested on June 1 on plunder and graft charges for allegedly receiving millions of pesos in kickbacks from flood control projects. /cb

World.title: DOJ: NBI to also probe death of Ateneo athletes
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Justice (DOJ) will see whether there is basis to file criminal charges in connection with the drowning of two members of the Ateneo de Manila University (ADMU) men’s basketball team while in a team-building activity in Aurora province.

In a statement on Wednesday, the DOJ said it has instructed the National Bureau of Investigation to form a task force that would look into the June 8 incident.

Article continues after this 

The DOJ promised to be “thorough, comprehensive and impartial” in the probe, which was announced a day after the Aurora provincial police ruled out foul play and called the drowning “purely an accident.”

“As part of its investigation, the NBI will determine whether there is sufficient basis to recommend the filing of charges before the DOJ,” it said. “The DOJ remains committed to ensuring that the facts are fully established and that justice is served.”

READ: PNP: Only 2 Ateneo coaching staff gave statements on players’ drowning

While parallel investigations are ongoing, speculations refused to die down regarding the sudden death of ADMU Blue Eagles rookie player Rene Baterbonia, 19, and Divine Adili, a 21-year-old Nigerian, in the waters off a beach resort in Barangay Lipit, Dipaculao town.

At a press conference on Tuesday, Police Col. Percival Pineda, the acting Aurora provincial police director, said the two players were wading through the water until they came to a deep area where they were suddenly swept by the current.

Article continues after this 

READ: PNP says Ateneo group 300 meters from resort, ‘asked to be alone’

Ateneo issued a statement late Tuesday, saying the remains of Baterbonia have been taken to Arlington Memorial Chapels and Crematory in Quezon City, while Adili’s body will be flown to Nigeria.

Article continues after this 

An autopsy will be conducted on Baterbonia at the request of his family, while the rest of the members of the ADMU men’s basketball team will undergo psychological intervention and counseling, ADMU said.

Aside from the Philippine National Police and the NBI, the local government of Dipaculao is also planning to conduct its own investigation into the incident.

Yet to speak with Tab

Also on Wednesday, Rovelyn Baterbonia, Rene’s mother who had earlier criticized the university on social media for the lack of information reaching the family about her son’s death, said she was not yet keen on pressing charges.

“For now, I will prioritize [the funeral] of my son before I [decide] on the next steps because I’m still waiting for the information [Ateneo] will provide me,” Baterbonia said at a press conference held by the Philippine Sports Commission.

Rovelyn noted that she had yet to receive any update on the autopsy done on Rene.

Three days after the deaths, she also has yet to speak with the Blue Eagles head coach, Tab Baldwin.

“Even if we face each other now, I don’t think I’d be able to speak with him because, as I said, I will attend to my son first. I will prioritize his funeral,” she said.

Also appearing at the press conference was Jimmy Bondoc, the singer-turned-lawyer known as a staunch supporter of former President Rodrigo Duterte.

‘Not to be disturbed’

Asked if Bondoc would be representing her should she decide to press charges, Rovelyn said it was Agusan del Sur Gov. Santiago Cane Jr. who had asked Bondoc and another Duterte counsel, Israelito Torreon, to study documents related to the incident.

Meanwhile, more details emerged on Wednesday about the day the players died.

Speaking to reporters at Camp Crame via teleconference, Pineda, the acting Aurora police chief, said the Ateneo team members were wading in the water “as part of their training”—in an area that was waist-deep and around 300 meters away from the resort grounds—around 2:40 p.m. on Monday.

“[They] asked to be left alone,” he said. “The team asked not to be disturbed. The activity was closed.”

Two players ‘rescued’

“The place they went to walk by the coastline was far from the resort front, around 300 meters. But the resort owner said it was safe in front of them and their lifeguard was there,” the police official added.

According to Pineda, there were two other players—whom he did not identify—who were swept by the current along with Baterbonia and Adili.

The two other players were rescued, but Baterbonia and Adili were found about 30 to 40 minutes later.

They were given first aid at the resort before being brought to a medical facility where they were pronounced dead, Pineda said.

He noted that the resort had adequate warning signs and other safety measures for water activities.

However, “based on our conversation with the resort owner, the team’s activity was kept exclusive,” Pineda said.

He also noted that “there was no coordination done with local government unit regarding the training.”

Baterbonia’s stated cause of death was “asphyxia by drowning,” Pineda added.

No bruises, weights

Quoting accounts from the town’s disaster management office, Pineda said the responders “did not see any weights on the (victims’) feet and hands, or any bruises when they were given first aid.”

As of Wednesday, investigators have yet to obtain statements from the victims’ teammates.

“Our investigators and police (in Aurora) tried to take their statements but … they were still in a state of shock,” Pineda said. “The ones who gave affidavits were the two coaching staff members. Those two were the ones sent to speak for them.”

World.title: Garin latest to sue Zaldy Co’s 18 ‘bagmen’ over kickback claims
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines — Iloilo Rep. Janette Garin on Wednesday became the latest public official to file cyberlibel charges against lawyer Levito Baligod and the 18 confessed former “bagmen” of resigned Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Elizaldy “Zaldy” Co over allegations linking her to supposed flood control kickbacks.

Garin lodged cyberlibel and perjury complaints before the Department of Justice (DOJ), three days after the group reiterated claims that they had delivered bags and suitcases of cash on behalf of Co to politicians and other personalities.

Article continues after this 

Speaking to reporters, Garin said the accusations appeared intended to “cripple me or prevent me from doing my task” as a member of the House leadership. Garin is a deputy speaker.

“Not one bag, envelope, or suitcase was given to me or any member of my family or office by Zaldy Co,” she said.

READ: Senate threat may involve Co’s ex-bagmen; report under validation – Gatchalian

Garin said she did not know any of the alleged bodyguards or drivers and maintained that her “conscience is clear.”

Growing list

Her complaint adds to a growing list of legal actions filed against Baligod and the 18 men, who first surfaced during a press conference at Club Filipino on Feb. 24, claiming they were ex-Marines and had served as Co’s bagmen in delivering cash allegedly sourced from anomalous flood control projects.

Article continues after this 

At least eight public figures have now filed cyberlibel or related complaints against the group.

On June 4, Iloilo City Rep. Julienne Baronda filed cyberlibel and perjury complaints after she was identified in the group’s affidavit as a supposed recipient of luggage containing cash.

Article continues after this 

Aside from Baligod, the other respondents in the complaints are Bernard Tube, Rosebert Waupan, Benny Bulontate, Johnny Buduan, Rodante Orbillo, Reyneboy Julian, Christopher Esquivel, George Villalon Jr., Romeo Rommel Bobares, Gil Navidad Jr., Anselmo Taberdo, Jowly Cadiao, Rommel Galapon, Cecilio Larroder Jr., Bernard Gumban, Crisaniel Dado, Fidel Corpu, and Walter Manalansan.

READ: 18 ‘ex-Marines’ at Senate to visit Padilla, not to attend BRC

On June 9, Manila Rep. Bienvenido “Benny” Abante Jr. filed libel and cyberlibel complaints, describing the allegations against him as “incorrect, baseless and misleading.”

On March 24, former Sen. Antonio “Sonny” Trillanes IV filed cyberlibel complaints over claims that he received $2 million from Co to bribe investigators of the International Criminal Court.

Also in March, Mamamayang Liberal Rep. Leila de Lima, Fr. Flaviano “Flavie” Villanueva, Bureau of Corrections Director General Gregorio Pio Catapang Jr., and former National Security Adviser Eduardo Año likewise filed complaints against the group, Baligod and former congressman Mike Defensor.

Senate hearing

The controversy resurfaced last week when Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano and his allies in the new minority convened the previous Senate blue ribbon committee and proceeded with a hearing where the 18 men repeated many of the allegations contained in an affidavit released in February.

Several lawmakers have since challenged the group’s claims.

Manila Rep. Joel Chua pointed to inconsistencies between the affidavit and the witnesses’ recent testimony, while former Palawan Rep. Jose Alvarez personally confronted the group at the Senate, denying that he had ever received cash-filled suitcases.

When asked why he was suddenly included in the list, Alvarez said it might be because of his refusal to endorse an impeachment complaint against President Marcos.

World.title: ‘Bagmen’ being probed for possible link to Senate security threat
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines — The Senate has tightened security after intelligence reports indicated that the 18 men who identified themselves as former “bagmen” of ex-Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Elizaldy “Zaldy” Co may be linked to a reported threat against the chamber.

Acting Senate President Sherwin “Win” Gatchalian said on Wednesday that information came from National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag, who briefed senators on intelligence reports suggesting a group may attempt to disrupt Senate operations.

Article continues after this 

“[Matibag] said there’s a possibility that there will be troublemakers in the Senate, and that they will be an armed group,” Gatchalian told reporters during a virtual press briefing.

Asked if the 18 men were among those being investigated, Gatchalian replied: “According to the NBI, it might be connected to them.”

READ: Tulfo rejects ‘18 Marines’ label, calls alleged bagmen ‘kargadors’

He stressed that the information remains under validation by intelligence agencies and is being consolidated by the National Intelligence Coordinating Agency (NICA).

The Senate has coordinated with the NBI, Philippine National Police and the Armed Forces of the Philippines to verify the reports.

Article continues after this 

Abundance of caution

As a precaution, the Senate placed its premises under heightened security, barred visitors from entering the complex, and implemented work-from-home arrangements for employees from June 10 to 11.

READ: 18 ‘ex-Marines’ at Senate to visit Padilla, not to attend BRC

Article continues after this 

“These measures are out of an abundance of caution,” Gatchalian said, emphasizing that legislative and administrative operations, including preparations for the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, would continue as scheduled.

“We have to take it seriously because my top priority is the safety of the employees, members of the media, and the senators,” he said.

Office of the Senate Sergeant-at-Arms chief Alfred Corpus said security personnel have intensified patrols and conducted security sweeps while awaiting feedback from law enforcement and intelligence agencies.

“The measures will be strictly enforced until the threat level is downgraded,” Corpus said.

The reported link surfaced as authorities continue investigating the 18 men, who emerged publicly in February claiming to be former Marines who served as bagmen for Co and delivered billions of pesos in alleged kickbacks from flood-control projects to government officials and lawmakers.

Ombudsman probe

The Office of the Ombudsman said its investigators would continue interviewing the group on Thursday as part of an ongoing fact-finding inquiry.

Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano said investigators would assess the credibility of the men’s allegations and determine which claims are supported by evidence.

“These types of details are considered confidential under our rules for fact-finding,” Clavano said when asked whether the interviews were related to the complaint against former Speaker Martin Romualdez.

The men have claimed they delivered P805 billion in alleged kickbacks from anomalous flood-control projects to several personalities, including Romualdez, who has repeatedly denied wrongdoing.

Defensor no-show at NBI

Meanwhile, former congressman Mike Defensor skipped a scheduled appearance before the NBI, calling a subpoena issued to him part of a “pattern of harassment.”

Defensor had been summoned over allegations that he offered P5 million to each of the 18 men in exchange for testimony related to the flood-control controversy. Through his lawyer, Ferdinand Topacio, he dismissed the accusations as hearsay. Matibag declined to comment.

Authorities have not disclosed further details about the reported threat, citing ongoing intelligence validation and security concerns.

Win asserts leadership

Gatchalian later assured Senate employees that salaries, benefits, and operational expenses would not be affected by the ongoing leadership dispute in the chamber. He said he had authorized the release of payroll for the Senate’s nearly 2,100 employees and maintained that chamber operations remain normal.

He also rejected proposals for a power-sharing arrangement, saying there is only one acting Senate leader recognized by the majority.

“There’s only one Senate President Pro Tempore. There’s only one designated acting Senate President and, therefore, since we were elected to do that, we will fulfill our role and ensure the Senate operations will not be stalled,” he told reporters.

Sen. Panfilo Lacson echoed the position, saying Senate employees should no longer be confused about whose directives to follow, noting that the Gatchalian-led majority bloc has been recognized by the Civil Service Commission and other government institutions.
